fastfetch.notes: Install, config path, run on shell start with a quiet-variable guard.
ASCII/ANSI text file with $1..$9 color slots, raw files, images via sixel/kitty/kitty-direct/iterm/chafa.
Key/title/separator colors and bar/percent colors; hex or ANSI names.

bat.notes: Built-in ansi/base16 follow the terminal; custom palettes via a generated .tmTheme + `bat cache --build`.

cava.notes: [color] gradient_color_1..8 (hex) bottom to top, horizontal_gradient_color_1..8, foreground/background.

clock-tui.notes: -c '#RRGGBB' or a named color; also default.color in config.toml.

delta.notes: syntax-theme ansi follows the terminal; diff backgrounds as hex styles; features group a look.

eza.notes: theme.yml with hex colors (needs a theme.yml-capable eza, 0.19+), or EZA_COLORS / LS_COLORS.

fd.notes: Colors from LS_COLORS only; generate it from palette tokens.

fzf.notes: --color with hex or ANSI names, or the base16 scheme to follow the terminal palette.

pipes-rs.notes: -c ansi follows the terminal palette; rgb mode uses built-in hue palettes, not the look palette.

pipes-sh.notes: -c INDEX per pipe color (repeatable); the hex comes from the terminal palette.

ripgrep.notes: --colors path/line/column/match/highlight with fg, bg, style; 24-bit via r,g,b.

rusty-rain.notes: -C rain, -H head, -G shade gradient, -B background; #RRGGBB or r,g,b.

tty-clock.notes: -C 0-7 picks an ANSI color; the hex comes from the terminal palette.

yazi.notes: Flavors (ya pkg add) or a theme.toml with hex colors; tmTheme for code preview.

zoxide.notes: No theme of its own. The `zi` picker is fzf: color it through FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS or _ZO_FZF_OPTS (see the fzf theme recipe).

atuin.notes: Interactive search, not inline ghost-text suggestions.

psreadline.notes: Predictive IntelliSense: inline or list view; needs PSReadLine 2.1+ (2.2+ for list view and plugins).

atuin.notes: Only syntax-highlights commands inside its search results (ui.syntax_highlight); not the command line you type.

zsh-autosuggestions.notes: Suggests from history as you type; no search UI. Use atuin or fzf for Ctrl-R.

iterm2.notes: Key mappings live in Settings > Keys (global) and Profiles > Keys (per profile, stored in the profile as a key map). The serialized format was not verified; set once in the UI and export the profile JSON, or use the Python API.

bash.notes: No syntax highlighting in plain readline; LS_COLORS drives ls and completion colors.

ble.sh.notes: Documents the cost; this is the tool's main drawback on Windows.

starship.notes: palettes + palette keys; named colors usable in any style string.

glazewm.notes: Tree of horizontal/vertical splits steered by the tiling direction; no named layouts and no automatic layout switching (community scripts exist).

tmux.notes: TPM (tmux plugin manager) installs git-hosted plugins.

zellij.notes: WASM/WASI plugins, Rust officially; built-in UI is itself plugins.

oh-my-posh.notes: nu, fish, zsh, PowerShell, cmd; bash needs ble.sh.

starship.notes: Native in PowerShell, fish and cmd/Clink; bash needs ble.sh; zsh and nushell are not built in.

oh-my-posh.notes: rprompt block: bash (ble.sh), zsh, PowerShell, cmd, nu, fish.

starship.notes: right_format works in elvish, fish, zsh, xonsh, cmd, nushell and bash (with ble.sh or Flyline); not listed for PowerShell.

bash.notes: PS1 + PROMPT_COMMAND; no native transient or right prompt.

fish.notes: fish_prompt / fish_right_prompt functions; fish_config prompt picks sample prompts.

nushell.notes: PROMPT_COMMAND / PROMPT_COMMAND_RIGHT closures and native TRANSIENT_PROMPT_* variables.

powershell.notes: function prompt {}; transient prompt via a PSReadLine Enter handler.

zsh.notes: PROMPT/RPROMPT with %-escapes, precmd hooks; transient prompt via ZLE hooks (starship/p10k provide it).

bash.notes: GNU Readline via ~/.inputrc; no built-in autosuggestions or syntax highlighting (ble.sh adds them, slow on Windows).

fish.notes: Autosuggestions, syntax highlighting, pager and abbreviations are built in.

nushell.notes: reedline: emacs/vi/helix, history hints, completion menus; syntax highlighting built in.

powershell.notes: PSReadLine. 5.1 ships 2.0.0 (no predictions); install >= 2.2 for prediction list view.

zsh.notes: ZLE built in; autosuggestions and syntax highlighting via zsh-autosuggestions / zsh-syntax-highlighting plugins.

nushell.notes: Built-in plus external completer closure (carapace, fish).

wezterm.notes: JetBrains Mono and Nerd Font Symbols are bundled.

alacritty.notes: Alacritty renders one glyph at a time and has no ligature support (maintainer statement in issue #50). Use WezTerm or Windows Terminal for ligatures.

foot.notes: The foot.ini(5) man page read has no ligature option (only `grapheme-shaping` under [tweak], for grapheme clusters). Foot is widely documented as not supporting ligatures, but that statement was not found in the pages fetched. Use kitty, Ghostty or iTerm2 for ligatures.

gnome-terminal.notes: No ligature key in the schema (enable-shaping is Arabic shaping only). Use kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty or iTerm2.

iterm2.notes: Enabling ligatures disables the GPU renderer.

konsole.notes: No ligature option in the profile keys read from Profile.cpp or in the handbook. Use kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty or iTerm2 for ligatures.

terminal-app.notes: The User Guide's Text settings list no ligature option. Use iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm or Ghostty.

alacritty.notes: No fallback list option. Missing glyphs come from OS font fallback, so use a patched Nerd Font as the main family.

gnome-terminal.notes: No fallback list; Pango/fontconfig supplies fallback glyphs. Use a patched Nerd Font as the main font, or install a symbols font system-wide.

iterm2.notes: Profiles > Text has a Non-ASCII font and Special Exceptions (range remap, with an Install Nerd Font Bundle option). Exact Dynamic Profile key names for these were not confirmed; configure once in the UI and export the profile as JSON to read them. Simplest path: use a Nerd Font as Normal Font.

konsole.notes: No fallback list. Konsole uses the system (fontconfig) fallback; the profile has a separate EmojiFont key (Appearance). Unverified that a symbols-only font is picked automatically for Private Use glyphs, so use a patched Nerd Font as the main font.

terminal-app.notes: No fallback list; macOS substitutes fonts per glyph. Use a Nerd Font as the main font for icons.

windows-terminal.notes: A comma-separated face list works; the docs describe face as a single name, so this relies on behaviour verified on Windows 11.

alacritty.notes: Only as an integer pixel offset (font.offset.y).

gnome-terminal.notes: The profile schema has no transparency key; the GNOME wiki FAQ says the option was removed from Preferences in 3.7. Ptyxis has a per-profile `opacity` key (org.gnome.Ptyxis.Profile, 0.0-1.0), or use kitty/WezTerm/Konsole/Alacritty.

alacritty.notes: window.blur works on macOS and KDE Wayland only; not on Windows or X11.

foot.notes: 1.26.0+, needs a build against wayland-protocols 1.45+ and a compositor with ext-background-effect-v1.

gnome-terminal.notes: No blur. Use Konsole, kitty, WezTerm or iTerm2.

wezterm.notes: Windows (Acrylic, Mica, Tabbed) and macOS work on stable; Wayland blur needs nightly; no blur on X11.

windows-terminal.notes: Acrylic per profile, Mica via a theme (Windows 11 build 22621+).

alacritty.notes: Not supported and not planned (maintainers closed the requests). Use WezTerm or Windows Terminal, or draw the art in a separate window layer.

ddterm.notes: No background image key in the settings schema. Use Guake, kitty, WezTerm or Konsole.

foot.notes: Not available; the config reference has no image option. Use alpha with a compositor-drawn wallpaper, or kitty/Ghostty/iTerm2 for images.

gnome-terminal.notes: No background image. Use Konsole, kitty, WezTerm or iTerm2.

windows-terminal.notes: Images are cached by path: a regenerated image needs a new file name.

alacritty.notes: No image or animation support. Use WezTerm or Windows Terminal.

foot.notes: No images or shaders. Use kitty (custom_shaders) or Ghostty (custom-shader).

ghostty.notes: No animated image formats; animate through a custom shader.

iterm2.notes: Only a static image (or a rotating folder of images) is documented for backgrounds. Use another terminal (Ghostty, kitty) for shader-driven animation.

kitty.notes: Via bundled or custom shaders (0.49+); animated image files are not documented.

konsole.notes: Wallpaper is a static image. Use kitty (custom shaders), Ghostty or WezTerm.

terminal-app.notes: Static images only. Use kitty, Ghostty or WezTerm.

wezterm.notes: Animated GIF or PNG layers animate only while the window has focus; costs GPU and VRAM. No video backgrounds.

windows-terminal.notes: backgroundImage accepts .gif but animated playback is not confirmed by the docs; a time-driven pixel shader (Time constant) is the reliable route.

alacritty.notes: No custom shader option. Windows Terminal (experimental.pixelShaderPath) supports shaders.

foot.notes: No shader support. Use Ghostty or kitty.

iterm2.notes: No custom shader support. Use Ghostty or kitty for shaders.

kitty.notes: custom_shaders, official since 0.49. Slang shaders, not GLSL.

konsole.notes: No shader support. Use Ghostty or kitty.

terminal-app.notes: No shader support. Use Ghostty or kitty.

wezterm.notes: No user shader hook is documented. Approximate with background layers (gradients plus image hsb dimming), or use Windows Terminal experimental.pixelShaderPath on Windows.

windows-terminal.notes: Experimental: experimental.pixelShaderPath (HLSL). Continued existence is not guaranteed by Microsoft.

gnome-terminal.notes: No padding key in the schema. Workaround: GTK CSS in ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css targeting VteTerminal padding (unverified here), or choose another terminal.

iterm2.notes: No padding setting in the Window profile docs. iTerm2 has Advanced settings for side and top/bottom margins (TerminalMargin, TerminalVMargin via `defaults write com.googlecode.iterm2`); names unverified here, check Settings > Advanced and search 'margin'.

terminal-app.notes: No padding setting in the User Guide's Text or Window panes. Use iTerm2 (margins) or another terminal.

alacritty.notes: No tabs on Windows or Linux by design; use tmux or zellij. macOS has native tab actions only.

foot.notes: No tabs. Use tmux/zellij, or one window per task under a tiling compositor.

iterm2.notes: Tab bar position and visibility are global preferences (Settings > Appearance > Tabs), not profile keys, so Dynamic Profiles cannot set them. A per-profile tab color exists (Colors tab) as `tab_color` in the Python API.

alacritty.notes: Full or None everywhere; Transparent and Buttonless are macOS only. No integrated tab bar.

iterm2.notes: Window style (normal, no title bar, full screen, ...) is the Style option in Settings > Profiles > Window; the Dynamic Profile key is `Window Type` (enum-backed number, values not confirmed). Export a profile to read the value for the style you want.

terminal-app.notes: Native title bar only. Profiles > Window > Title chooses what the title shows (working directory, path, process name, dimensions...), not the chrome. For a borderless look use another terminal.

alacritty.notes: No splits by design; use tmux or zellij.

foot.notes: No built-in splits. Use tmux/zellij or compositor tiling.

gnome-terminal.notes: No split panes. Use tmux/zellij, or Ptyxis/Konsole.

terminal-app.notes: No independent split panes. Terminal has a Shell > Split Pane command, but user reports describe it as a second view of the same session, not a new shell (not confirmed in Apple's docs). Use tabs, tmux or zellij.

alacritty.notes: No drop-down mode. Use an OS-level launcher or window-manager rule, or Windows Terminal (quakeMode) on Windows.

foot.notes: No drop-down mode. Set `app-id` and use a compositor scratchpad or window rule (compositor-specific, unverified), or use kitty's quick-access-terminal.

ghostty.notes: Quick terminal. Linux needs Wayland + wlr-layer-shell.

gnome-terminal.notes: No drop-down mode. On GNOME use ddterm (Shell extension) or Guake, both in this catalog.

iterm2.notes: Hotkey window is created through the UI; Dynamic Profile keys for hotkeys were not confirmed.

konsole.notes: Konsole has no drop-down mode. The KDE drop-down terminal is Yakuake, a separate app that embeds Konsole and uses Konsole profiles and color schemes.

terminal-app.notes: No drop-down mode. Use iTerm2's hotkey window.

wezterm.notes: No built-in drop-down or quake window is documented. Use an OS-level launcher or window-manager rule, or Windows Terminal (quakeMode action) on Windows.

alacritty.notes: No OSC 133 prompt marks or directory tracking features. Use WezTerm or Windows Terminal.

terminal-app.notes: No configurable shell integration in the User Guide. Terminal sets TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal and macOS's zsh startup tracks the working directory for it (community knowledge, not verified here).

alacritty.notes: Single window, single shell. Run tmux or zellij with a layout file as the shell command (see default-shell recipe).

foot.notes: No sessions or layouts. Start a multiplexer layout with `shell=`/command, or set `initial-window-size-chars`.

ghostty.notes: No session or layout file. Use tmux/zellij for pane layouts, `window-width`/`window-height` for size, or the macOS AppleScript dictionary (listed on the features page) to script windows and tabs.

gnome-terminal.notes: No layout or session file. gnome-terminal(1) accepts per-launch options (such as --tab, --window, --working-directory and profile selection; not re-read here), or use tmux/zellij.

iterm2.notes: Window arrangements (Window > Save Window Arrangement; restore at launch via Settings > General > Startup) and the Python/AppleScript APIs. Not expressible as a plain config file; format not verified.

alacritty.notes: No Sixel, iTerm2 or Kitty image protocol. Use WezTerm or Windows Terminal (Sixel).

foot.notes: Sixel. The kitty and iTerm2 image protocols are not documented.

ghostty.notes: Kitty graphics protocol. Sixel is not documented.

terminal-app.notes: No inline image protocol is documented. Use iTerm2, kitty or WezTerm.

wezterm.notes: iTerm2 image protocol (wezterm imgcat) is documented. Sixel and Kitty graphics support level is not confirmed here.

windows-terminal.notes: Sixel only; no iTerm2 or Kitty image protocols.

alacritty.notes: No profiles. Run alacritty --config-file <file> or -o 'key=value' per use case, or import shared files with general.import.

foot.notes: No profiles. Use `foot -c <file>`, `include=` in foot.ini, or `-o section.key=value` per launch.

ghostty.notes: One config, no profile concept. Use `config-file = ?other` includes or launch with a different `--config-file`.

kitty.notes: No profile concept. Use `include other.conf` plus `kitty --config <file>` or `-o key=value` per launch, and session files for tab/window setups.

wezterm.notes: No profile concept. launch_menu entries and domains (WSL, SSH) fill the role.

foot.notes: No live reload; restart foot (in server mode restart the server). Runtime color theme switching works: key bindings color-theme-switch-dark / color-theme-switch-light / color-theme-toggle, or SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 to the foot process.

bat.notes: fzf preview, MANPAGER, git, cat alias, delta.

fzf.notes: fd as the walker, bat/eza previews, per-shell wiring.

lazygit.notes: delta diff renderer, editor, Nerd Font icons, shell alias.

ripgrep.notes: fzf live grep, delta/bat as viewers.

yazi.notes: `y` wrapper that changes directory on exit, optional dependencies.

zoxide.notes: cd replacement, fzf picker, yazi/other tools that read the database.

cava.notes: Bars, widths, framerate, orientation, smoothing, input method; -p for a per-pane config file.

cbonsai.notes: Flags only: live/infinite/screensaver, growth speed, life, branching, geometry, leaves.

clock-tui.notes: Size, seconds, date, timezone, mode (clock, timer, stopwatch, countdown).

cmatrix.notes: Flags only: speed (-u), bold, asynchronous scroll, message, screensaver mode.

pipes-rs.notes: Pipe kinds, count, delay, turn chance; flags or config.toml.

pipes-sh.notes: Flags only: pipe count, type, framerate, straightness, reset.

rusty-rain.notes: Character group, direction, speed, shade; flags in the pane command.

tty-clock.notes: Flags only: seconds, date, box, centering, blink, refresh.

aerospace.notes: AeroSpace deliberately has no window borders. Companion tool: JankyBorders (brew tap FelixKratz/formulae; brew install borders), macOS 14+. Start it from AeroSpace by adding to ~/.aerospace.toml: after-startup-command = ['exec-and-forget borders active_color=0xffRRGGBB inactive_color=0xffRRGGBB width=5.0'], with active_color = the look's {palette.accent} and inactive_color = {palette.ansi.brightBlack}, each written as 0xff followed by the hex without the #. Colors are 0xAARRGGBB.

glazewm.notes: Focused and non-focused window border colors via window_effects, Windows 11 only. Border width is not configurable.

i3.notes: Width and colors only. Rounded corners need an external X11 compositor.

sway.notes: Width and colors only. No rounded corners in sway itself (SwayFX adds them).

yabai.notes: yabai has no window border option in the current docs. Companion tool: JankyBorders (brew tap FelixKratz/formulae; brew install borders), macOS 14+. Add as the last line of yabairc: borders active_color=0xffRRGGBB inactive_color=0xffRRGGBB width=5.0 &, with active_color = the look's {palette.accent} and inactive_color = {palette.ansi.brightBlack}, each written as 0xff followed by the hex without the #. Colors are 0xAARRGGBB.

i3.notes: for_window and assign cover float, size, position, border and workspace. There is no opacity command; transparency needs a compositor.
